blocks.text: Design a frontend flow where an AI-generated proposal remains reviewable advice until the user confirms a permitted product action. Expose evidence freshness and uncertainty, preserve user edits, reconcile versioned outcomes, and never turn generated text into authority.

What you are solving:
A proposal-to-action UI for reviewing affected records, inspecting evidence, editing selection, confirming a high-impact command, and recovering from mixed per-item results.

Decision surface:
- Which proposal facts and evidence are inspectable?
- How does stale or incomplete evidence change available actions?
- Which state is generated, locally edited, optimistic, or authoritative?
- How are version conflicts and partial outcomes reconciled?
- How do safe rendering, cancellation, accessibility, and feedback work?

steps.title: 1. Request proposal
steps.text: Capture user intent and show cancellable pending work without blocking unrelated product tasks.

steps.title: 2. Review evidence
steps.text: Render a structured proposal with affected items, evidence freshness, uncertainty, limitations, and allowed capabilities.

steps.title: 3. Edit and confirm
steps.text: Keep selection and edits in local ReviewState; require explicit confirmation for high-impact actions against the current proposal version.

steps.title: 4. Reconcile outcomes
steps.text: Merge authoritative per-item success, failure, and conflict results, then keep recovery beside failed items.

blocks.title: Clarifying questions
items: What product decision is the proposal helping with?
Which records, evidence, permissions, and versions must be visible?
Which actions are reversible, destructive, or unavailable?
Can the user edit scope before confirmation?
When does a proposal expire or require refreshed evidence?
How should partial command outcomes be recovered?

blocks.title: Review safety and user-control expectations
items: Pending AI work does not block unrelated tasks.
Generated content is rendered as untrusted data.
Stale evidence disables confirmation without erasing review context.
Command retry is idempotent and version-aware.
Uncertainty and mixed results are understandable without color alone.

blocks.title: AI-assisted workflow states
rows: Show cancellable progress and preserve request intent
Slow work does not look like a frozen page
Show proposal, evidence, limitations, and editable affected items
Suggestion remains distinct from user authority
Explain missing freshness or permission and disable confirmation
Visible text cannot grant a capability
Show pending command followed by per-item results
A success headline cannot hide failures

items.label: Primary UX goal
items.helperText: Generated proposals never execute by presentation alone.

items.label: Latency UX
items.helperText: Capabilities change when evidence becomes stale or unavailable.

items.label: Resilience
items.helperText: Mixed results remain accurate and recoverable.

blocks.title: Scope checkpoint
blocks.text: The core design separates AIProposal, ReviewState, UserDecision, PendingCommand, and authoritative Outcome. Cancellation only stops local waiting unless the action contract confirms otherwise.

The frontend owns intent capture, uncertainty presentation, review controls, cancellable pending work, safe defaults, feedback, provenance display, and accessible state changes. Server-side model selection, inference, policy evaluation, and product mutations remain authoritative behind abstract proposal and action contracts.
